clue.text: Unexpected changes in Virginia –- good sign

parts.note: VA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
Aries is a sign of the zodiac, the Ram

explanation.surface: Someone notes sudden shifts in Virginia, taken as a lucky omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are whims or erratic shifts, things that alter without warning.

clue.text: Wine: quantity upset over trainee

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: a sum is an amount or quantity
a cadet is a trainee, as in the forces or police

explanation.surface: A wine buff complains that a quantity of wine was knocked over by a clumsy trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Met man working in foster care?

indicators.note: working means the letters of the following words are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Metropolitan Police officer might be employed in the foster care system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met man' suggests a London policeman (the Met is London's police force), but here it means a man from the Met Office, Britain's weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecaster works for the Met Office, the UK's meteorological service.

clue.text: Tinker with instrument

definitions.meaning: to tamper or meddle with something

explanation.surface: Tinkering with a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: fiddling about with something, and the fiddle as a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Call number — doctor needs to go round

definitions.meaning: to ... a number is to telephone it
to ... a stolen car is to doctor its identity so it can be sold on

explanation.surface: A caller is told the doctor needs to make a house visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; here it is a verb, as in British slang for disguising a stolen vehicle with false plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one verb: telephone, falsify a stolen car's identity, and encircle.

clue.text: Deceptive showman's trick on panellist

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a juror sits on a jury panel

explanation.surface: A tricky entertainer plays a prank on a member of a quiz panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician performing illusions is a showman whose act depends on deceiving the audience.

clue.text: Fixed interference affecting TV

definitions.meaning: the crackle or snow of electrical interference on a broadcast

explanation.surface: A repair person has sorted out the interference spoiling the television.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, and is also the noise from atmospheric electrical interference.

clue.text: Former partner raised fare to go on American flight

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is lifted to read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do is to fare, as in 'how are you doing?'
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An ex-partner has paid the fare for a flight on an American airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price but is the verb: to do or get on.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a fleeing of many people.

clue.text: Dog set sail around UK!

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
set means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a dog has set sail to travel around Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set sail' reads as a phrase about a voyage, but 'set' is the anagram signal, giving SALI, which then wraps the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern hunting hound, a breed of greyhound type.

clue.text: Sister, apprehensive initially, in college in Warwickshire town

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Eton is the famous school, Eton College

indicators.note: initially says take just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A nervous nun turns up at a college in a Midlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in north Warwickshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Monitor head of welterweight boxer, perhaps after disturbing chat

indicators.note: after means the dog comes after the rearranged letters
head of means take the first letter of the next word
disturbing means the letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, so a dog by example

explanation.surface: A boxing commentator keeps an eye on the welterweight's head as the fighter is put off by trash talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' wants to be a fighter, matching 'welterweight', but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a body or person keeping a check on others, a guardian against abuses.

clue.text: 'Sole' used in pun I queried

indicators.note: used in says the answer's letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone queries a pun on the word sole, as in the fish or the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and unique both mean the only one of its kind.

clue.text: One has intuition of horror filling man who's sent into pit

indicators.note: filling means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a miner works down a coal pit
dread is fear or horror

explanation.surface: Someone senses the dread of a man about to be sent down a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepath is supposed to know others' thoughts, a gift close to intuition.

clue.text: Go mad, crackers, teaching

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is driven mad by teaching that is utterly crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is doctrine or a set of teachings laid down as true.

clue.text: Well-placed? Rather, after session

indicators.note: after means the first word listed comes behind the next piece

parts.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or for a portrait
pretty means rather or fairly, as in pretty good

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are in a fairly good position after a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a comfortable or advantageous position is idiomatically to be well placed.

clue.text: Shared home of little value

parts.note: in means at home
common means ordinary or cheap

explanation.surface: A shared house that is worth very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Things held jointly by people are possessed together, owned mutually.

clue.text: Green light for doctor entering in this way at Oxford, say

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: thus means in this way
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
to be up is to be in residence at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Approval for a doctor to be admitted to Oxford this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for at university is a British usage: students go up to Oxford and come down when they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up and a green light are both idioms for permission to go ahead.

clue.text: Key-operated device Ivy League university rugby player's used

parts.note: Yale is one of the US Ivy League universities
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: An Ivy League rugby player uses a gadget opened with a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yale lock is a cylinder lock opened by a flat key, a brand name now generic.

clue.text: Legless, British before game

indicators.note: before means the first piece is placed ahead of the next

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A British player was drunk before the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, not missing limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang words for being extremely drunk.

clue.text: Part of season ticket to be paid for at a later date

definitions.text: to be paid for at a later date

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the cost of a season ticket can be settled later.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying on tick is a British idiom for buying on credit, paying later.

clue.text: Cover in many pieces loony left tackling Labour's leader

parts.note: loony means crazy

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so this piece wraps around the other

parts.note: quit means left, as in left a job

indicators.note: leader means take the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A cover story: a crazed left-winger takes on the leader of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A patchwork bedspread of irregular scraps of fabric sewn together is a kind of quilt.

clue.text: End of July, too soon for annual

indicators.note: End of says take the final letter of the next word

parts.note: early means too soon, before the due time

explanation.surface: The end of July is too early for an annual event.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual and yearly both describe something happening once every year.

clue.text: Shakespearean king, likewise holding on

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: also means likewise

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king does the same thing and clings on.
explanation.definitionFit: Alonso is the King of Naples in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: To show willing, take part in dance

parts.note: to play is to take part, as in a game
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: To show eagerness, you join in at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for co-operating, being willing to go along with others.

clue.text: Stay for start of play

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: start of says take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Remain until the beginning of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb meaning remain; it is the noun for a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a support or brace, as a prop is.

clue.text: One cuts weeds in street verge attended by this person, right?

parts.note: a rim is an edge or verge
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A gardener tidies roadside weeds, attended by the speaker, asking for confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verge' suggests the grass strip by a road, where a strimmer works; here it just means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered line trimmer used to cut grass and weeds, a British trade name.

clue.text: Start a filling meal

indicators.note: filling means the small word goes inside the other

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Begin a hearty, satisfying meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' looks like it describes a hearty meal; it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to start it off, as with a campaign or product.

clue.text: Be quick to appear fashionable

parts.note: to look is to appear, as in look tired
snappy means smart or stylish, as a snappy dresser

explanation.surface: Hurry up to appear stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: To look snappy is an idiom urging someone to hurry up.
